user_prompt: What is the effect of intranasal steroids (e.g. mometasone, beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone), with or without other treatments given equally to both arms, compared with no steroid treatment (no treatment, or the same co-treatment alone), on persistence of otitis media with effusion (OME) in children at up to 1 month?  Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR) using a random-effects model. RR < 1 means fewer children/ears with persistent effusion in the steroid arm (favours steroids).  Outcome: number with persistent middle ear effusion at the first assessment up to 1 month (≤ 6 weeks) after starting treatment, extracted as event counts per arm (events and total for steroid and control). - Persistence = effusion still present at follow-up: tympanogram type B (or type C2 / non-type-A if that is how the study defines failure), "not cured", "no improvement", or "persistent effusion". Resolution/cure = type A tympanogram or complete clearance. If a study reports resolution or improvement, convert it to persistence as total minus resolved. - If the headline result is a multi-category or ordinal scale (e.g. complete remission / partial remission / no change / exacerbation), do not discard the study. Look for a table of post-treatment tympanogram types or cure/no-cure counts per arm and derive persistence counts from it. - Unit of analysis: use children if reported per child. If results are reported per ear, use ears and combine right and left ears (sum both ears' events and totals). Never use one ear only. - If a trial has more than two arms, use only the intranasal-steroid arm and the no-steroid arm that received the same co-treatment. Ignore oral-steroid, montelukast, antihistamine-only or other active arms.  Do not pool hearing thresholds/air-bone gap, symptom or parent-reported improvement, quality of life, adverse events, or results after 6 weeks. Exclude oral or systemic steroid trials and trials whose control arm is a placebo spray.
